title: 02. Ingestion & Chunking: Fixed-Size Chunking (Character and Token-Based)
summary: Fixed-size chunking splits documents into segments of a predetermined size — either by character count or token count — with an optional overlap between consecutive chunks.

sections.title: ① Concept Explanation
sections.body: Fixed-size chunking splits documents into segments of a predetermined size — either by character count or token count — with an optional overlap between consecutive chunks. It is the simplest and fastest chunking strategy, requiring no semantic understanding of the text. Character-based splitting uses byte/character counts, making it model-agnostic. Token-based splitting counts tokens using the specific tokenizer of the target LLM (via `tiktoken` for OpenAI models), ensuring chunks never exceed context window limits. Fixed-size chunking is the baseline approach and works well for homogeneous, well-structured text, but fails at sentence boundaries — a chunk may end mid-sentence, cutting critical context.

diagrams.title: Why chunks overlap
diagrams.mermaid:
flowchart LR
  T["…returns need proof of purchase within 30 days…"] --> A["chunk 1: …returns need proof of"]
  T --> B["chunk 2: proof of purchase within 30 days…"]
  A -. "overlap keeps the phrase whole in chunk 2" .- B
diagrams.explain: Fixed-size splitting cuts text at arbitrary positions. **Overlap** (typically 10–20% of the chunk size) repeats the boundary text in both neighbours, so a sentence that crosses the cut is still retrievable in one piece. Too much overlap wastes storage and returns near-duplicate chunks.

sections.title: ④ Visual Explanation
sections.body:
```
FIXED-SIZE CHUNKING — BOUNDARY PROBLEM AND FIX
════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

PROBLEM: Character-based splitter cuts mid-sentence
────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
Original text (250 chars):
"The warranty covers manufacturing defects for two years from
 the date of purchase. Customers must retain proof of purchase
 for warranty claims to be processed."

chunk_size=100, overlap=0:
  Chunk 1: "The warranty covers manufacturing defects for two year"
                                                            ▲ CUT
  Chunk 2: "s from the date of purchase. Customers must retain pr"
            ▲ incomplete word                              ▲ CUT  
  Chunk 3: "oof of purchase for warranty claims to be processed."

→ Chunk 1 and 2 are USELESS — broken words, no meaning

FIX: RecursiveCharacterTextSplitter with sentence separators
────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
chunk_size=150, overlap=30, separators=["\n\n", "\n", ". ", " "]:

  Chunk 1: "The warranty covers manufacturing defects for two years
            from the date of purchase."
            ← ends at sentence boundary ✓

  Chunk 2: "Customers must retain proof of purchase for warranty
            claims to be processed."
            ← starts at sentence boundary ✓

OVERLAP VISUALIZATION:
────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
Text:    |----A----|----B----|----C----|----D----|
chunk 1: |----A----|----B----|
chunk 2:           |--B--|----C----|      (30 char overlap on B)
chunk 3:                    |--C--|----D----|  (30 char overlap on C)

→ Every boundary region B and C appears in TWO chunks
→ Even if query matches the boundary, full context is available

TOKEN COUNT vs CHARACTER COUNT:
────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
Language       Chars    Tokens   Ratio
English        1000     ~250     0.25 tok/char
Chinese        1000     ~500     0.50 tok/char  
Code (Python)  1000     ~400     0.40 tok/char
HTML/XML       1000     ~150     0.15 tok/char (lots of tags)

→ ALWAYS use token-based splitting for LLM pipelines
→ Character splitting is only safe for model-agnostic storage
```

quiz.question: What is the difference between character-based and token-based chunking, and when does it matter?
options: Chunk size selection is empirical — there's no universal answer.
Root Cause: Fixed-size character splitter cut at a character boundary in the middle of a sentence.
For Chinese/Japanese characters, 1 character = 1-3 tokens (vs 0.25-0.5 tokens/char in English).
Character-based chunking splits on character count (e.g., 1000 chars).
quiz.explanation: Character-based chunking splits on character count (e.g., 1000 chars). Token-based chunking splits on token count using the LLM's tokenizer. It matters because: (a) LLM context windows are measured in tokens, not characters; (b) token:character ratio varies — code might be 1 token/char, while whitespace-heavy text is 0.2 tokens/char; (c) for OpenAI models, exceeding the token limit raises an error.

quiz.question: What is chunk overlap and why is it important? What are the tradeoffs of too much vs too little overlap?
options: Chunk size selection is empirical — there's no universal answer.
Root Cause: Fixed-size character splitter cut at a character boundary in the middle of a sentence.
For Chinese/Japanese characters, 1 character = 1-3 tokens (vs 0.25-0.5 tokens/char in English).
Chunk overlap is the number of characters/tokens shared between consecutive chunks.
quiz.explanation: Chunk overlap is the number of characters/tokens shared between consecutive chunks. It ensures that context spanning a chunk boundary is captured in at least one complete chunk. Too little overlap (0-5%): sentences split across boundaries are truncated, losing critical context at boundaries.

quiz.question: How do you choose the right chunk size for your use case?
options: Chunk overlap is the number of characters/tokens shared between consecutive chunks.
Root Cause: Fixed-size character splitter cut at a character boundary in the middle of a sentence.
For Chinese/Japanese characters, 1 character = 1-3 tokens (vs 0.25-0.5 tokens/char in English).
Chunk size selection is empirical — there's no universal answer.
quiz.explanation: Chunk size selection is empirical — there's no universal answer. Guidelines: Short, factual Q&A (FAQ): 256-512 tokens. Users ask precise questions needing precise short answers.

quiz.question: How does tokenization differ for multilingual text and how does this affect chunk sizing?
options: Chunk size selection is empirical — there's no universal answer.
Root Cause: Fixed-size character splitter cut at a character boundary in the middle of a sentence.
Chunk overlap is the number of characters/tokens shared between consecutive chunks.
For Chinese/Japanese characters, 1 character = 1-3 tokens (vs 0.25-0.5 tokens/char in English).
quiz.explanation: For Chinese/Japanese characters, 1 character = 1-3 tokens (vs 0.25-0.5 tokens/char in English). Always use token-based chunking for multilingual corpora. Test: tiktoken.encode("这是中文") vs tiktoken.encode("This is English") — similar character count, very different token count.
